bottleneck: Textbook plasticity rules like spike-timing-dependent plasticity were derived from brain slices and paired recordings, but whether and how they operate in the intact, behaving brain is uncertain. In vivo, neuromodulators gate plasticity, dendritic computation complicates the pre/post spike picture, and credit assignment across millions of synapses has no agreed mechanism — backpropagation is biologically implausible, and no alternative is validated. The brain learns continuously from sparse data; we do not know the learning rule it uses. This ignorance caps both neuroscience and brain-inspired AI.
current_state: Three-factor learning rules and dendritic theories are proposed, but no plasticity framework is validated in the behaving mammalian brain. The learning rule remains unknown.

title: In vivo synaptic learning rules unknown
why_it_blocks: Understanding how brains learn is the foundation of education, rehabilitation, and AI. Without the true learning rule, brain-inspired computing copies the architecture while missing the algorithm that makes it work.
